ubo_and_aml_profiling.statutory_law_governance: Law of the People's Republic of China on Anti-Money Laundering (revised 2024, effective January 1, 2025); Measures for the Administration of Beneficial Owner Information by Financial Institutions and Specific Non-Financial Institutions (PBOC/SAMR Order No. 3, effective November 1, 2024); Company Law of the People's Republic of China (2023 revision); Foreign Investment Law of the People's Republic of China (effective January 1, 2020); Provisions on the Administration of Registration of Market Entities; Measures for the Registration of Foreign-Invested Enterprises in China; CSRC and PBOC rules on customer due diligence; UN Security Council sanctions implementation regulations and MOFCOM sanctions lists.

mandatory_notarization_and_apostille_bun.document_name: Certificate of Incorporation or equivalent registration certificate of foreign parent entity
mandatory_notarization_and_apostille_bun.issuing_entity: Competent company registrar in the jurisdiction of incorporation of the foreign investor
mandatory_notarization_and_apostille_bun.authentication_path: Notarization by a local notary public in the country of origin, followed by issuance of a Hague Apostille certificate by the competent authority designated under the 1961 Hague Apostille Convention; no Chinese consular legalization required if the country of origin is an Apostille Contracting State. The apostilled document must then be translated into Chinese by a certified translation agency and submitted to the Chinese market regulator; the original apostille and translation must be presented for verification.

mandatory_notarization_and_apostille_bun.document_name: Certificate of Good Standing of foreign investor
mandatory_notarization_and_apostille_bun.issuing_entity: Company registry or competent corporate registry authority of the foreign investor's home jurisdiction
mandatory_notarization_and_apostille_bun.authentication_path: Notarization plus Hague Apostille (or consular legalization if the home jurisdiction is not party to the Apostille Convention), followed by certified Chinese translation and submission to the local SAMR MOFCOM or notarization filing office.

mandatory_notarization_and_apostille_bun.document_name: Board Resolution or Power of Attorney authorizing incorporation of the WFOE and appointment of its legal representative
mandatory_notarization_and_apostille_bun.issuing_entity: Board of directors of the foreign investor company or authorized corporate body
mandatory_notarization_and_apostille_bun.authentication_path: Corporate resolution notarized and sealed in the country of origin, then apostilled or consular legalized as legally required; certified Chinese translation must accompany the application documents filed with the market regulation authority.

mandatory_notarization_and_apostille_bun.document_name: Articles of Association / Memorandum of Association of the foreign investor
mandatory_notarization_and_apostille_bun.issuing_entity: Foreign investor company and its home-jurisdiction registrar
mandatory_notarization_and_apostille_bun.authentication_path: Certified copy with apostille or consular legalization, plus certified Chinese language translation; submitted as part of the establishment application dossier to the SAMR district office and the foreign-investment information reporting system.

mandatory_notarization_and_apostille_bun.document_name: Bank Reference Letter for the foreign investor
mandatory_notarization_and_apostille_bun.issuing_entity: A recognized banking institution in the foreign investor's home jurisdiction
mandatory_notarization_and_apostille_bun.authentication_path: Original or certified copy, notarized if required, apostilled/consular legalized where applicable, translated into Chinese, and retained for bank account opening and capital verification purposes.

ubo_and_aml_profiling.pep_and_sanctions_screening_protocols: The WFOE's ultimate beneficial owners, legal representative, directors, supervisors, senior managers, foreign investor, and any individual exercising effective control must be screened against the UN Security Council consolidated sanctions list, OFAC SDN and non-SDN lists, EU consolidated sanctions lists, China's MOFCOM and MFA sanctions and unreliable entity lists, PBOC money-laundering risk lists, and domestic PEP databases. Enhanced due diligence is mandatory for any politically exposed person or entity with direct or indirect ownership, control, or significant business relationships. Screening must be refreshed before each transaction and at least every 90 days; negative news and adverse regulatory findings must be escalated to the AML compliance officer. If any sanction match or PEP linkage is identified, transaction approval requires senior management and legal counsel sign-off, with suspected illegal activity reported through the PBOC suspicious transaction reporting system.

statutory_name_clearance_protocol.registry_portal_name: China National Enterprise Credit Information Publicity System (National Enterprise Credit Information Publicity System) and SAMR Online Name Registration System / State Administration for Market Regulation Enterprise Registration Portal
statutory_name_clearance_protocol.language_and_transliteration_doctrine: The Chinese company name must be in Simplified Chinese characters and must be composed according to the statutory four-tier structure: administrative division + distinctive trade name + industry or business characteristic + enterprise legal form. The trade name may not be identical or confusingly similar to an already registered enterprise name nationwide or within the same industry and region. A foreign-invested enterprise may also use a transliterated or corresponding Chinese trade name derived from the investor's foreign name, but all names must comply with Measures for the Administration of Enterprise Name Registration. English names are not independently registered; they may be used in business documentation if the Chinese name is registered. Phonetic transliteration from Roman script to Chinese characters is not generally permitted as a standalone name except as a recognized transliteration trade name; the chosen Chinese characters must not violate public interest, morality, or contain misleading content. Nationwide uniqueness screening is applied to the trade name segment within the same industry, with exception for wholly foreign-owned enterprises if the foreign investor's own registered trademark or well-known trade name is used with consent.
statutory_name_clearance_protocol.extension_and_rejection_appeal_sop: Upon receiving a formal rejection from the SAMR enterprise name registration system, the applicant must first request in writing the specific statutory ground for refusal and the exact conflicting registered name or trademark. The applicant may then file an administrative reconsideration application with the market regulation administration at the next higher level within 60 days of the rejection notice, or alternatively file an administrative lawsuit with the competent people's court within six months. The appeal should include the reserved name filing number, a corrected proposed name with a revised four-tier structure, supporting evidence that the rejected name is not identical or confusingly similar, and any prior trademark registration or parent-company name priority evidence. If the ground relates to a prohibitive character, the applicant must delete or replace the offending token. For ministerial approvals on sensitive names, the applicant should coordinate with the local SAMR office and obtain pre-clearance from the relevant ministry. All correspondence must be in Simplified Chinese, and the applicant should preserve time-stamped submission records. If the rejection is based on rights held by a third party, the applicant may also engage in private consent or objection proceedings. For unresolved disputes, judicial review under the Administrative Procedure Law is available.

registered_office_and_commercial_substan.virtual_office_permissibility: A virtual office or commercial mailbox without a physical presence is generally not permissible as the sole registered office for a WFOE in China. The Market Entity Registration Regulations and the Company Law require a fixed and legitimate business address that is actually owned or leased by the enterprise, verifiable by the local SAMR, tax authority, and banks. Municipal tax authorities and banks routinely reject virtual offices because the WFOE must maintain substantive business premises for VAT invoice verification, tax inspection, labor contract filing, customs registration, and financial audit. For the manufacture of handmade sharp-edge epoxy resin liquid core RPG polyhedral dice, a physical production and warehousing facility is indispensable; a virtual office is operationally untenable and would expose the company to cancellation of registration, tax abnormality designation, bank account restrictions, and legal liability. A mail-forwarding service may be used only as an auxiliary address, never as the sole registered address. The registered address must match the business license, tax registration, and bank account records, and any relocation must be filed before the municipal SAMR and tax authority.
registered_office_and_commercial_substan.physical_inspection_likelihood: Checklist: 1) Lease agreement and property ownership certificate or permit for the registered address; 2) on-site photographs of the production workroom, storage shelves, epoxy casting benches, ventilation systems, and fire-safety equipment; 3) payroll and social insurance records for employees physically working at the premises; 4) production equipment invoices and raw material purchase contracts; 5) electricity, water, and logistics usage records consistent with manufacturing activity; 6) trademark, product samples, and sales contracts demonstrating the actual business line; 7) personal interviews with the legal representative and production supervisors. Quantified risk: High, approximately 60-70% within the first 24 months of operation, especially under the 2024 SAMR crackdown on 'shell' and 'zombie' enterprises. Municipal tax authorities conduct targeted inspections of newly registered WFOEs in manufacturing sectors at a rate of at least 20-25% in high-compliance districts; if any VAT anomaly or invoice mismatch appears, the likelihood of unannounced physical inspection rises to above 80%. Noncompliance may trigger deregistration, tax abnormal status, and revocation of the business license.

incorporation_legal_framework.governing_statute_and_sections: Company Law of the People's Republic of China (2023 Revision, effective 1 July 2024), Articles 14, 16, 23, 27, 30, 31, 34, 38, 43, 44, 46, 47, 49, 51, 59, 60, 62, 63, 67, 68, 71, 72, 75, 80, 84, 91, 93, 95, 97, 246; Foreign Investment Law of the People's Republic of China (2020), Articles 2, 4, 6, 9, 12, 14, 20; Regulations on the Implementation of the Foreign Investment Law (2020), Articles 8, 17, 20; Interim Provisions on Market Entity Registration Administration (2021), Articles 2, 8, 13, 15, 19
incorporation_legal_framework.competent_registry_authority: State Administration for Market Regulation (SAMR) and the provincial or municipal Market Supervision and Administration Bureau where the WFOE's registered office is located; the integrated enterprise registration window also transmits the foreign investment information report to the Ministry of Commerce (MOFCOM)
incorporation_legal_framework.statutory_filing_instrument: Market Entity Registration Application Form for a Foreign-Invested Company, submitted together with the Articles of Association and the Foreign Investment Information Report
incorporation_legal_framework.minimum_paid_up_capital_rule: None. No national minimum paid-up capital is applied to a WFOE limited liability company in the toy and game manufacturing sector. The sole foreign shareholder must subscribe the full registered capital in the Articles of Association, and under Company Law Article 47, the subscribed capital must be fully contributed within five years from establishment. No blocked escrow or special capital holding account is required for this industry; foreign capital must be remitted through a disclosed foreign exchange capital account and used strictly within the approved business scope.

step_by_step_formation_sop.step_name: Proposed Company Name Reservation and Foreign Investment Negative List Pre-screening
step_by_step_formation_sop.competent_authority: SAMR National Enterprise Name Reservation Portal connected to the local Market Regulation Bureau; MOFCOM foreign investment negative list screening through the same integrated e-registration window
step_by_step_formation_sop.detailed_action_protocol: Submit one primary and at least three alternative legal person names through the national enterprise name reservation portal operated by SAMR and connected to the local Market Regulation Bureau. The proposed name should follow the combination of administrative division, distinctive brand, industry descriptor, and limited company to avoid identical or confusingly similar registered marks. Before reserving the name, the foreign investor must verify that the business scope of manufacturing tabletop role-playing dice is not on the Foreign Investment Negative List; if outside the list, only an information report is required at the later registration stage. Complete investor identity verification, beneficial ownership declaration, and anti-money laundering KYC screening, and ensure the foreign investor's passport and corporate standing documents are notarized and legalized where necessary. Retain the name reservation notice for submission in the registration application.
required_dossiers: Foreign investor passport or equivalent identity certificate
Proof of foreign investor nationality and residence address
Certificate of corporate existence and director register if investor is a legal person
Proposed Chinese company names, with at least three alternatives
Notarized authorization letter appointing the local filing agent if utilized
Brief statement of investment purpose, projected business scope, and capital contribution plan
step_by_step_formation_sop.adverse_action_remedies: If the name is rejected for duplication, prohibited characters, or similarity to an existing trademark, file an amended name submission within three working days through the same portal. If the negative list screening flags the business scope, obtain a written negative list exemption or industry approval from the relevant competent ministry, or amend the business scope to exclude the restricted activity before continuing. Any KYC insufficiency should be cured by submitting updated passport copies, bank references, or beneficial ownership declarations within three working days after query.

step_by_step_formation_sop.step_name: Company Formation Filing, Foreign Investment Information Report, and Business License Application
step_by_step_formation_sop.competent_authority: Provincial or municipal Market Supervision and Administration Bureau through the integrated enterprise registration portal; MOFCOM receives the Foreign Investment Information Report electronically through this integrated system
step_by_step_formation_sop.detailed_action_protocol: Execute the Articles of Association, the sole shareholder's written decision, and the first board resolution. Submit the Market Entity Registration Application Form through the integrated enterprise registration portal, including the foreign investment information report. Indicate the registered capital amount, contribution method, and five-year contribution schedule in accordance with Company Law Article 47. Appoint the legal representative, executive director or board, supervisor, general manager, and financial controller. Attach notarized and legalized identity documents of the foreign investor, the local lease file for the registered office, and the name reservation notice. The registration authority issues a unified social credit code and a five-in-one business license after examination, covering tax registration, statistics, social insurance, and customs-related registration codes where applicable.
required_dossiers: Market Entity Registration Application Form
Articles of Association signed by the sole foreign shareholder or its authorized representative
Sole shareholder's written decision and first board resolution
Notarized and legalized foreign investor identity or corporate standing documents
Copy of the enterprise name reservation notice
Lease agreement, landlord identity certificate, and property ownership proof for the registered office
Consent of the landlord permitting enterprise registration at the site
Foreign Investment Information Report form
Appointment documents for legal representative, supervisor, directors, and executive officers
step_by_step_formation_sop.adverse_action_remedies: If the Market Regulation Bureau issues a correction notice, respond with the missing or corrected documents within 15 working days; failure to respond will be treated as withdrawal. If the application triggers negative list review, apply for a special industry approval or adjust the business scope to a negative-list-free activity. If notarization or legalization is defective, re-execute the documents at the embassy, consulate, or notary office and resubmit within 10 working days. No production or sales activity should commence before the business license is obtained.

step_by_step_formation_sop.step_name: Post-Registration Seals, Tax Registration, Payroll, Customs, and Foreign Exchange Registration
step_by_step_formation_sop.competent_authority: Public Security Bureau licensed seal engraving houses; local State Taxation Administration branch; local social insurance and housing fund offices; local customs office and State Administration of Foreign Exchange (SAFE) branches
step_by_step_formation_sop.detailed_action_protocol: After obtaining the business license, apply at a Public Security Bureau licensed engraving house for the company seal, financial seal, invoice seal, and legal representative seal, and file the seal impressions with the local Public Security Bureau. Complete tax registration using the unified social credit code, activate electronic invoice capacity, and register the payroll, social insurance, and housing fund plans. If the WFOE will export dice sets or import epoxy resin raw materials, complete customs registration, foreign trade operator filing, and the export-import record at the local customs authority. Complete the SAFE foreign exchange registration for the capital account and operating foreign exchange account, and maintain the statutory books and registers at the registered office. The financial controller is responsible for preparing the initial accounting policy, chart of accounts, and capital contribution records.
required_dossiers: Business license with unified social credit code
Legal representative identity certificate and appointment resolution
Company seal, financial seal, invoice seal, and legal representative seal filing records
Tax registration and electronic invoice capacity application form
Bank account information or bank application reference before final account opening
Customs registration and foreign trade operator filing forms if export or import is intended
SAFE foreign exchange registration forms and capital account application documents
Employment contracts and social insurance registration schedules for initial employees
step_by_step_formation_sop.adverse_action_remedies: If tax registration is not activated or invoicing capacity is rejected, submit a corrected tax information form and proof of address to the local tax service hall within five working days. If custom registration is delayed, use the express correction window and provide the business license, unified social credit code, and lease agreement. If the SAFE registration is questioned, submit the articles, board resolution, and source-of-funds proof and request a re-examination via the SAFE online system; no foreign currency capital remittance should be received before the capital account registration is approved.

step_by_step_formation_sop.step_name: Bank Account Opening and Foreign-Currency Registered Capital Injection
step_by_step_formation_sop.competent_authority: A commercial bank lawfully authorized to provide foreign exchange services, together with the local SAFE branch responsible for capital account registration and foreign exchange monitoring
step_by_step_formation_sop.detailed_action_protocol: Open the basic deposit account, general deposit account, and foreign exchange capital account at a bank authorized to handle foreign exchange. The bank will verify the business license, articles, seal register, legal representative identity document, and board resolution. Complete the SAFE foreign exchange registration for the capital account and then cause the sole foreign shareholder to remit the subscribed registered capital into the foreign exchange capital account. The capital contribution must be made in accordance with the filed schedule and the Company Law's five-year rule. After receipt, foreign exchange settlement shall follow the actual needs principle, and settled funds must be used only for approved operating expenses, raw materials, rent, wages, and service fees within the business scope. The financial controller must maintain a capital contribution ledger and provide bank statements and capital verification materials to the auditor or notary public if required.
required_dossiers: Business license and unified social credit code certificate
Articles of Association and first board resolution
Seal registration card and legal representative identity document
SAFE capital account registration form
Application for basic deposit account and foreign exchange capital account
Bank signatory forms and specimen seal cards for all authorized signatories
Capital contribution schedule and source-of-funds statement
Lease agreement proving the physical business address
step_by_step_formation_sop.adverse_action_remedies: If the bank raises KYC or beneficial ownership questions, provide an updated corporate ownership chart, bank references, and source-of-funds evidence within 10 working days. If SAFE registration is suspended, correct the application and provide the missing board resolution or capital schedule, then re-submit through the SAFE online portal. If the bank rejects the foreign capital remittance, use another authorized bank and pre-clear the remittance instruction with the bank compliance department; do not use personal accounts for any registered capital contribution.

step_by_step_formation_sop.step_name: Industrial and Environmental Licensing, Fire Safety Approval, Occupational Health, and Product Certification
step_by_step_formation_sop.competent_authority: Municipal Bureau of Ecology and Environment; Fire and Rescue Section of the local Emergency Management Bureau; local Occupational Health and Safety administration; CNCA-accredited certification bodies for China Compulsory Certification; local Market Supervision Administration for product quality and consumer safety
step_by_step_formation_sop.detailed_action_protocol: Identify the environmental impact assessment classification for the production facility under the MEE Classified Management List for Environmental Impact Assessment. For a small, manually operated epoxy resin dice casting workshop using less than ten tonnes of resin and hardener per year and discharging no process wastewater except domestic sewage, file an EIA Registration Form online at the municipal EIA filing system. If resin or solvent consumption exceeds the registration threshold or the process creates significant volatile organic compound emissions, submit an EIA Report Form and obtain approval before construction or operation. Simultaneously submit fire protection design and completion acceptance filing to the Fire and Rescue Section, including evacuation routes, fire separation, and separate storage for epoxy resin and hardeners. Engage a qualified body to conduct occupational hazard monitoring for epoxy vapor, sharp-edge finishing noise, and manual handling. If the tabletop dice are classified as toys intended for children under 14, apply for and obtain China Compulsory Certification under the toy product catalogue before placing them on the Chinese market.
required_dossiers: Business license and approved business scope
EIA Registration Form or EIA Report Form and approval documents if required
Lease agreement and property ownership certificate
Factory floor plan with production, mixing, storage, and finishing areas identified
Fire protection design and completion acceptance filing documents
Fire alarm, extinguisher, and emergency exit inspection records
Material Safety Data Sheets for epoxy resin, hardener, pigments, and cleaning agents
Occupational hazard monitoring report and hazard factor registration
Emergency response plan for chemical spills and fire
China Compulsory Certification application and product safety test reports if toys are made for sale to children under 14
step_by_step_formation_sop.adverse_action_remedies: If the online EIA registration fails the consistency check, amend and resubmit within 10 working days. If the authority requires a full EIA Report, hire a licensed environmental assessment institute, conduct public participation, and submit the report within 30 working days. If fire inspection identifies noncompliance, install the required fire suppression systems, reroute storage, and request a re-inspection within 30 working days. If product testing shows that the dice fall under the toy CCC catalogue, obtain the certificate before production for domestic sale; until certification is granted, no product may be supplied within China.

national_tax_registration_infrastructure.competent_tax_authority: State Taxation Administration (STA) of the People's Republic of China, acting through the electronic tax filing portal known as the Electronic Tax Bureau (e-Tax Bureau), accessible at etax.chinatax.gov.cn, with the China International Trade Single Window used for export clearance integration.
national_tax_registration_infrastructure.tax_id_procurement_sop: For a Wholly Foreign-Owned Enterprise (WFOE) limited liability company in mainland China, the tax identification procedure is as follows: (1) Incorporate the company with the State Administration for Market Regulation (SAMR) and obtain the Unified Social Credit Code, which serves as the de facto Tax Identification Number for tax registration; (2) Within 30 days after issuance of the business license, complete tax registration at the local competent tax authority office of the STA by filing the taxpayer registration questionnaire, legal representative identity documents, articles of association, registered address proof, and bank account information; (3) Receive the official tax registration certificate and complete the taxpayer classification determination; (4) Apply for general taxpayer status or remain a small-scale taxpayer depending on projected annual turnover; (5) Activate the electronic tax filing account on the Electronic Tax Bureau portal and link the Unified Social Credit Code; (6) For VAT and export-related purposes, apply for the export tax refund and exemption registration through the electronic portal; and (7) Obtain any required digital certificates (U-key or e-tax seal) for encrypted electronic filing and digitalized electronic invoice issuance.

indirect_taxation_nexus_and_rules.statutory_registration_threshold_local_c: Mandatory VAT registration for all WFOEs upon establishment; general VAT taxpayer registration is mandatory when annual aggregate taxable turnover (from sales of goods, services, or imports) exceeds RMB 5,000,000. Below this threshold, small-scale taxpayer simplified VAT rates apply unless the taxpayer voluntarily elects general taxpayer status.
indirect_taxation_nexus_and_rules.electronic_invoicing_and_clearance_manda: China operates the Golden Tax Phase IV system and the fully digitalized electronic invoice (digital e-invoice) clearance mandate. VAT invoices must be issued through the STA-controlled e-invoice platform, with real-time encrypted reporting and automatic one-click upload to the tax authority's central database. Special VAT invoices must include the digital anti-fraud tax control code, and all voided or corrected invoices must be reported under the same system. Full digitalized electronic invoices are integrated with the e-Tax Bureau and require API-based or portal-based issuance with real-time validation before the invoice is legally recognized for input VAT crediting and customs export rebate purposes.

export_zero_rating_and_refund_substantia.zero_rating_eligibility: Exported tabletop roleplay polyhedral dice manufactured by the WFOE qualify for zero rating of VAT under Chapter 5 of the PRC VAT Implementing Regulations, provided the goods actually leave mainland China through an approved customs clearance point and the seller is a registered general VAT taxpayer that has completed export tax exemption and refund filing. The export sale must be properly declared in the export customs declaration, with all goods physically shipped abroad, and the sales proceeds must be received in foreign currency and repatriated to the enterprise's domestic bank account through the official cross-border foreign exchange settlement system.
mandatory_customs_documentation_bundle: Customs Export Declaration (customs clearance declaration submitted through the China International Trade Single Window)
Commercial invoice issued by the exporting WFOE
Special VAT invoice for export (if applicable) or export-invoice documentation supporting zero-rated treatment
Original Bill of Lading or air waybill evidencing shipment to the overseas consignee
Export proceeds receipt record and bank foreign exchange collection confirmation from the approved settlement bank
Export contract or sales order and any packing list or certificate of origin required by the importing jurisdiction
export_zero_rating_and_refund_substantia.audit_scrutiny_and_clawback_penalties: The State Taxation Administration has full audit authority to verify export zero-rating claims, using cross-referencing of customs export data, electronic invoicing data, and bank foreign exchange settlement records. If any export transaction is found to be fraudulent, unsubstantiated, or not accompanied by genuine foreign exchange repatriation, the tax authority will claw back the entire VAT input credit or export rebate previously granted, impose a late-payment surcharge of 0.05% per day of the underpaid tax, and may impose an administrative fine of 50% to five times the evaded tax amount. In severe cases of deliberate false export declarations involving forged bills of lading or fabricated export contracts, the matter is referred to criminal authorities under the PRC Criminal Law for smuggling and tax fraud penalties, including imprisonment.

fx_control_regime_and_central_bank_regul.central_bank_authority: People's Bank of China (PBOC) and State Administration of Foreign Exchange (SAFE)
fx_control_regime_and_central_bank_regul.currency_convertibility_assessment: China maintains a regulated hybrid convertibility system. Current-account transactions, including trade-related import/export payments, service payments, and post-tax profit remittances by a Wholly Foreign-Owned Enterprise (WFOE), are substantially convertible provided that the underlying transaction has a genuine commercial basis, supporting documents are presented, and the domestic settlement bank reports the transaction to SAFE. Capital-account transactions remain tightly controlled; inbound equity subscriptions, foreign-currency loans, and liquidation proceeds require SAFE registration, pre-approval, or post-event filing, with banks refusing payments that lack a valid foreign-exchange purpose code and matching economic reality. For a WFOE manufacturing tabletop gaming dice, an important surrender-related concern is that export proceeds in foreign currency must be repatriated into a licensed domestic bank account and either retained or sold for RMB within prescribed trade-monitoring windows; funds cannot remain indefinitely offshore. Profit remittance is treated on the current side, but the bank will require audited financial statements, the annual corporate income tax return, the China tax clearance certificate, a board resolution approving the dividend, and evidence that the RMB funds were lawfully converted before the outbound remittance. Overall, the RMB is not freely convertible in the capital sense, but operationally the WFOE can circulate cash between its CNY and foreign-currency accounts through licensed banks once every transaction is documented and reported.
fx_control_regime_and_central_bank_regul.export_proceeds_surrender_rules: Under the current SAFE trade monitoring framework, China no longer imposes a mechanical fixed-percentage forced surrender of export proceeds. Export receipts from the sale of RPG dice and gaming accessories must be repatriated to a licensed domestic bank account, generally within 180 days from the applicable export declaration date unless the bank approves a longer verified commercial payment term. Once received, the WFOE may retain the foreign currency in its current-account foreign-exchange settlement account up to the bank-approved cap or may voluntarily sell it to the bank for RMB at the prevailing onshore rate. The account cap is established by the bank based on the enterprise's verified annual trading volume, and any retention beyond the cap must be converted or removed through a valid underlying transaction. All export proceeds, including funds collected through PayPal and Stripe platform aggregators before settlement into the corporate bank account, must be traceable to genuine sales orders, customs declarations, logistics documentation, and platform settlement reports.

tier1_domestic_commercial_banks.bank_name: Bank of China (Head Office, Shanghai Branch Accepting WFOE Accounts)
tier1_domestic_commercial_banks.account_class: Capital Escrow Account / Basic Operational Currency Account

tier1_domestic_commercial_banks.bank_name: Industrial and Commercial Bank of China (ICBC)
tier1_domestic_commercial_banks.account_class: Capital Escrow Account / Basic Operational Currency Account

corporate_banking_onboarding_blueprint.fintech_emi_cross_border_viability: Low viability. Offshore digital EMI platforms such as global neobanks and non-licensed fintech payment companies are legally barred from serving as the primary treasury account holder for a mainland Chinese WFOE because China requires all cross-border trade and capital-account settlements to flow through PBOC-licensed banks integrated with SAFE reporting. Foreign fintech EMIs cannot issue mainland account numbers, cannot receive RMB settlement, and cannot satisfy SAFE regulations on trade verification, anti-money-laundering, and capital controls. Third-party service providers such as Stripe, PayPal, and cross-border payment gateways may only be used as downstream collection channels for B2C consumer payments; their aggregated proceeds must then be remitted to the WFOE's licensed domestic corporate bank account, accompanied by transaction-level settlement and e-commerce documentation. No unlicensed digital institution can replace a Tier-1 Chinese commercial bank for capital escrow, foreign-exchange settlement, or corporate liquidity management.
corporate_banking_onboarding_blueprint.physical_presence_and_kyc_interview_mand: Chinese banks, applying PBOC customer due diligence rules, require the WFOE's legal representative and at least one authorized officer to physically appear in-branch for the on-boarding interview, original passport or identity card presentation, and execution of bank-account opening documents. Remote or consular-proxy opening is generally not accepted for a newly incorporated WFOE, especially where the ultimate beneficial owner is a non-resident foreign shareholder. If the foreign statutory director is outside China, most state-controlled commercial banks will permit a physically present local general manager or a Chinese-resident authorized signatory holding a notarized power-of-attorney to complete the in-person KYC interview, provided that (a) the power-of-attorney is notarized in the director's home country and apostilled or consular-legalized, (b) the company seal and statutory board resolution are verified, and (c) all original corporate documents are presented at the branch. After the physical meeting, ongoing transaction instructions can be submitted through corporate internet banking with dual-approval controls, but any change of legal representative or authorized signatory requires a new physical verification exercise.

critical_aml_kyc_blockers_and_defense.trigger_point: Shareholder-chain opacity: the bank identifies a Hong Kong or BVI intermediate holding company and cannot complete the ultimate beneficial ownership (UBO) assessment for the foreign parent of the Chinese WFOE.
critical_aml_kyc_blockers_and_defense.evidentiary_defense_dossier: Notarized corporate organizational chart covering every intermediate entity; certificate of incorporation and registered agent certificate for each intermediate holding company; register of directors and shareholders of each entity; completed PBOC-style beneficial ownership declaration form; audited financial statements of the ultimate foreign parent; sworn statement confirming no UBO is a politically exposed person, sanctioned individual, or sanctioned entity; apostilled board resolution authorizing the WFOE formation.

critical_aml_kyc_blockers_and_defense.trigger_point: Inbound equity injection is flagged as a high-risk lump-sum capital movement because the initial paid-in capital substantially exceeds the projected operating expenses and revenue trajectory for a low-risk tabletop gaming accessories manufacturer.
critical_aml_kyc_blockers_and_defense.evidentiary_defense_dossier: Capital contribution board resolution and amended shareholders agreement; detailed five-year business plan and cash-flow projection; fixed-asset purchase agreements for resin molding equipment, epoxy raw materials, and quality-testing instruments; CFO sign-off on capital deployment schedule; SAFE-issued Foreign Direct Investment (FDI) registration receipt; original source-of-funds documentation from the foreign investor's bank, including dividend records, retained earnings statements, or sale-of-assets contracts proving lawful funding.

critical_aml_kyc_blockers_and_defense.trigger_point: E-commerce settlement mismatch: deposits from PayPal and Stripe arrive from numerous overseas buyers but the bank cannot match them to customs declarations, causing concern about export-receipt concealment, trade falsification, or indirect money laundering.
critical_aml_kyc_blockers_and_defense.evidentiary_defense_dossier: Corporate PayPal Business and Stripe Merchant ID verification letters; daily platform settlement statements and transaction-level sales logs; invoice numbering and order data exported from the e-commerce system; logistics airway bills and courier tracking reports; customs export declarations with the corresponding HS head and matched quantities; refund, chargeback, and dispute register; statement of e-commerce platform terms of service; internal AML declaration explaining that direct-to-consumer tabletop dice shipments may have low unit values and high frequency.

critical_aml_kyc_blockers_and_defense.trigger_point: Overseas trade disbursements to related-party suppliers or to low-tax jurisdictions trigger transfer-pricing and trade-based money-laundering red flags during outbound payment review.
critical_aml_kyc_blockers_and_defense.evidentiary_defense_dossier: Signed master supply agreement and purchase orders with clear Incoterms; beneficiary bank documentation; bills of lading, airway bills, or courier receiving evidence; customs clearance certificates for imported resin pigments, molds, and packaging; quality inspection reports issued by the factory; OECD-compliant transfer pricing documentation and a contemporaneous Supported Transaction in a Chinese comparability study; board minutes explaining the commercial rationale for selecting each overseas vendor; confirmation that all beneficiary names and account numbers match the underlying trade contracts.

cross_border_liquidity_and_clearing_rail.inbound_capital_injection_routing: Inbound equity capital must be wired from the foreign shareholder's own overseas bank account to the WFOE's designated capital account at a licensed domestic bank using SWIFT MT103 or fast-payment cross-border messaging. The remittance instruction must cite a SAFE-recognized purpose code in the Direct Investment category for Inbound Foreign Direct Investment Equity Capital Injection. The WFOE must first complete the SAFE basic information registration under the Foreign Direct Investment system and obtain an FDI number, after which the bank deposits the funds into a foreign-currency capital escrow account. For every inward remittance, the corporate treasury must preserve the capital injection notice, the board resolution authorizing the funding amount, the foreign investor's certificate of incorporation, and the source-of-funds evidence. Upon receipt, the bank conducts currency convertibility by allowing the enterprise to sell the incoming foreign currency for RMB at the onshore rate or to retain it within the capital account subject to SAFE conditions. The WFOE then engages a registered Chinese CPA to issue a capital verification report confirming the paid-in registered capital, and the same evidence is used to update SAFE and the market regulation authority. All RMB conversion from the capital account is separately reported under SAFE's capital settlement system and must be applied only to lawful operating expenditures within the WFOE's business scope.
cross_border_liquidity_and_clearing_rail.outbound_trade_disbursements: Outbound trade payments for imported raw materials, molds, packaging, licensing fees, and overseas operational services should be routed through the WFOE's current-account settlement bank using SWIFT MT103 for direct wire payments up to approved trade limits. For higher-value or recurring procurement contracts, a Commercial Letter of Credit (L/C) issued via SWIFT MT700 provides secure settlement by matching bank documents against sales contracts and shipping evidence. Documentary Collections remain available for fixed business partners where the WFOE and the overseas supplier agree on bank-mediated documents against payment or acceptance; the bank will require invoices, purchase orders, bills of lading/airway bills, customs declarations, and evidence that the foreign beneficiary is a genuine operating counterparty. When the WFOE repays overseas shareholder loans or distributes dividends, separate board resolutions, tax clearance certificates, audited financial statements, and form-based SAFE declarations are mandatory. All outbound payments must be made from the lawful foreign-currency or RMB funds in the corporate account; payments cannot be executed against unverified third-party instructions, and the bank applies economic-sanctions screening against UN, EU, US OFAC, and Chinese sanctions lists before each transfer.
permissible_fx_hedging_instruments: Onshore deliverable RMB/FX forward contracts concluded with the licensed Chinese commercial bank, with tenors generally from T+1 to 12 months, supported by verified current-account net exposure or approved capital-account cash-flow exposure, including rolling window forwards for recurring trade settlements.

Non-deliverable forwards (NDFs) for a mainland WFOE are generally impermissible as an onshore instrument; Chinese residents cannot access the offshore NDF market, so treasury hedging is limited to deliverable CNY forwards, with any NDF-type risk layering allowed only through the ultimate foreign parent operating outside mainland China.

RMB/FX currency swaps and cross-currency interest-rate swaps are available through licensed domestic banks for matched principal and interest flows, but only where the swap is tied to an actual trade or investment liability, the maturity aligns with the underlying exposure, and the transaction carries no speculative or speculative arbitrage motive.

annual_compliance_calendar_matrix.receiving_authority: State Administration for Market Regulation (SAMR) via the National Enterprise Credit Information Publicity System
annual_compliance_calendar_matrix.statutory_deadline_window: January 1 to June 30 of each year, covering the immediately preceding calendar year
annual_compliance_calendar_matrix.delinquency_sanctions: Failure to file within the window triggers inclusion in the List of Enterprises with Abnormal Operations; if not remedied within three years, inclusion in the List of Enterprises with Serious Illegal/Unreliable Behaviors (blacklist), causing five-year disqualification of the legal representative, restriction on bank acceptance, mandatory de-registration/administrative strike-off, and loss of business license.

annual_compliance_calendar_matrix.statutory_deliverable: Corporate Income Tax Annual Final Settlement (Annual CIT Return)
annual_compliance_calendar_matrix.receiving_authority: Local competent tax authority, State Taxation Administration (STA)
annual_compliance_calendar_matrix.statutory_deadline_window: On or before May 31 of the year following the tax year
annual_compliance_calendar_matrix.delinquency_sanctions: Late payment surcharge of 0.05% per day on unpaid tax, late-filing fine of RMB 50 to RMB 20,000 (or 50% to 500% of underpaid tax for fraudulent misdeclaration), tax lien order, asset seizure, freezing of bank accounts, and possible criminal liability for tax evasion.

annual_compliance_calendar_matrix.receiving_authority: Ministry of Commerce (MOFCOM) and SAMR via the integrated annual report platform
annual_compliance_calendar_matrix.statutory_deadline_window: January 1 to June 30 annually, co-filed with the SAMR annual report
annual_compliance_calendar_matrix.delinquency_sanctions: Corrective order and fine up to RMB 100,000 for failure to file or material misrepresentation; adverse foreign-exchange special management, rejection of cross-border fund settlement, loss of preferential treatment under the Foreign Investment Law, and impeded future changes to registered capital or shareholding.

annual_compliance_calendar_matrix.statutory_deliverable: Annual Statutory Audit Report of Financial Statements
annual_compliance_calendar_matrix.receiving_authority: Company shareholders and board; retained on file for SAMR and STA inspection
annual_compliance_calendar_matrix.statutory_deadline_window: Within five months after fiscal year end (by May 31 for calendar-year companies), before the Annual CIT filing and the annual shareholders' approval meeting
annual_compliance_calendar_matrix.delinquency_sanctions: Audited statements not prepared and approved in time may invalidate dividend distributions, result in rejection of the annual CIT filing, trigger regulatory penalty for unverified financial statements, expose directors to civil liability, and enable shareholder derivative claims.

annual_compliance_calendar_matrix.statutory_deliverable: Annual Beneficial Ownership Confirmation and Update
annual_compliance_calendar_matrix.receiving_authority: SAMR via the beneficial ownership information module of the annual report
annual_compliance_calendar_matrix.statutory_deadline_window: January 1 to June 30 annually, with a mandatory 30-day post-event filing window for any change in beneficial ownership (share transfer, new control rights)
annual_compliance_calendar_matrix.delinquency_sanctions: Non-disclosure or false disclosure results in a fine up to RMB 50,000 for individuals and RMB 100,000 for companies, plus corrective orders; chronic non-compliance triggers inclusion in the abnormal-operations list and secondary restrictions on foreign exchange and banking transactions.

statutory_audit_and_accounting_mandate.compulsory_audit_thresholds: Under the PRC Company Law, PRC Accounting Law, and the Foreign Investment Information Reporting Rules, an independent statutory audit by a licensed CPA firm is mandatory for: (1) any wholly foreign-owned enterprise (WFOE) incorporated in mainland China, regardless of size; (2) any enterprise with annual operating revenue exceeding RMB 30 million; (3) any enterprise with total assets exceeding RMB 50 million; (4) any enterprise with an annual average workforce of 200 or more; (5) any enterprise applying for enterprise income tax non-resident benefits, tax offsets, or carrying forward tax losses; (6) any enterprise engaged in financial, insurance, securities, or public-interest activities; and (7) any enterprise whose articles of association or binding shareholder resolution mandates an external audit. The audit must be executed in accordance with China Certified Public Accountant Auditing Standards.
statutory_audit_and_accounting_mandate.governing_accounting_framework: PRC Accounting Standards for Business Enterprises (ASBE), which are substantially converged with International Financial Reporting Standards (IFRS); eligible small and micro enterprises may apply the Simplified Small Enterprise Accounting Standards, although foreign-invested enterprises are ordinarily expected to apply full ASBE for statutory reporting and tax reconciliation.

corporate_registers_and_ubo_annual_confi.ubo_annual_confirmation_protocol: The PRC Measures for the Management of Beneficial Ownership Information (effective 2024) require each company to maintain a true and current register of every individual directly or indirectly holding 25% or more of equity, voting rights, or effective control. Any change in shareholding or control must be filed with SAMR within 30 days of the event. Annually, the WFOE must confirm the accuracy of its beneficial ownership data through the Annual Enterprise Information Disclosure Report (filed January 1 to June 30), and must simultaneously verify that the corporate registers (members, directors, supervisors, charges) reflect all transfer deeds, pledges, and board resolutions passed during the year.

recurring_annual_maintenance_budget_usd.registered_office_or_agent_market_range_: USD 500 – 1,500 per annum (registered office address plus corporate secretarial/registered agent services – typical for a WFOE in major Chinese cities)
recurring_annual_maintenance_budget_usd.statutory_audit_estimated_fee_usd: USD 2,000 – 8,000 per annum (standard certified audit for a small to mid-size WFOE with usual transactional volume and clear accounting records)

corporate_income_tax_regime.effective_tax_rate_incentives: Small low-profit enterprises are taxed at an effective 5% rate on taxable income up to RMB 3 million under the current preferential inclusion rule (25% of taxable income included at the 20% statutory small-enterprise rate). High and New Technology Enterprises may access a 15% preferential rate. Qualifying R&D expenses enjoy a 100% additional super-deduction. Certain encouraged foreign-invested industries operating in designated western regions or free-trade zones may obtain a 15% CIT rate or temporary tax holidays, subject to substantive business activity conditions.

tax_return_filing_anatomy.form_identifier_and_portal: PRC Enterprise Income Tax Annual Return (Form A100000), filed electronically through the State Administration of Taxation e-Taxation portal (electronic tax filing system) by the WFOE as the taxpayer resident in China.
tax_return_filing_anatomy.reporting_frequency: Quarterly provisional filing followed by the annual consolidated settlement return. Quarterly returns are due within 15 days after the end of each quarter; the annual return is due before 31 May of the following tax year.
tax_return_filing_anatomy.statutory_deadline_rule: The annual corporate income tax return and the final payment of tax must be filed within 5 calendar months after the end of the tax year. Quarterly provisional returns are filed within 15 calendar days after the end of each quarter and provisional tax is paid at the same deadline.

field_by_field_filling_dissection.entry_description: Gross sales revenue from the production and sale of handmade sharp-edge epoxy resin liquid core RPG polyhedral dice, including Kickstarter pre-sales, Stripe/PayPal e-commerce sales, wholesale distribution, and export sales.
field_by_field_filling_dissection.non_resident_entry_guidance: Report all sales to foreign related parties, including a related-party overseas distributor, at the independent arm's-length price supported by a transfer pricing study. Unjustified price discounts to a Hong Kong or offshore affiliate will be adjusted under PRC Enterprise Income Tax Law Article 41, with the revenue reallocated into China at 25 percent.

field_by_field_filling_dissection.entry_description: Direct manufacturing costs attributable to epoxy resin liquid cores, polyhedral moulds, pigment additives, packaging materials, production labour, and factory overheads.
field_by_field_filling_dissection.non_resident_entry_guidance: For purchases of resin or mould-making services from foreign related suppliers, the WFOE must document the negotiated price by reference to the CUP or Cost Plus method. Failure to price intercompany purchases at arm's-length may lead to downward revision of the deductible cost and a compensating adjustment on the related-party transaction, together with interest and penalties.

field_by_field_filling_dissection.entry_description: Deductible Chinese VAT surcharges, including city maintenance and construction tax and education surcharges, associated with domestic taxable sales of dice products.
field_by_field_filling_dissection.non_resident_entry_guidance: Export sales are generally VAT-zero-rated or export-rebated and should not generate recoverable surcharges. The WFOE must segregate local taxable turnover from export turnover. Foreign platform fees are not recorded in this line and cannot be used to inflate surcharge deductions.

field_by_field_filling_dissection.entry_description: Kickstarter campaign fees, Stripe/PayPal transaction charges, e-commerce platform commissions, online advertising spend, freight/logistics costs, and trade promotion expenses.
field_by_field_filling_dissection.non_resident_entry_guidance: Only fees actually incurred and paid for services rendered to the WFOE are deductible. If fees are paid to a non-resident affiliate for intangible marketing rights, the payment may be deemed a royalty subject to 10% withholding tax and to transfer pricing review. A payment lacking economic substance or beneficial ownership will be recharacterized as a dividend.

field_by_field_filling_dissection.entry_description: Management salaries, social insurance contributions, office rent, legal and accounting fees, depreciation of production equipment, and enterprise-level overheads.
field_by_field_filling_dissection.non_resident_entry_guidance: Directors' salaries must be supported by actual employment records and PRC social insurance obligations. Excessive management fees or head office cost allocations paid to a foreign parent or brother company are not automatically deductible and must satisfy the arm's-length standard and the actual-service test under CIT Law Article 41 and SAT Announcement No. 42 of 2016.

field_by_field_filling_dissection.entry_description: Interest on shareholder advances, bank loan interest, currency exchange losses, and financial handling fees incurred in the ordinary course of funding the WFOE's dice-casting operations.
field_by_field_filling_dissection.non_resident_entry_guidance: Interest paid to a non-resident controlling shareholder is subject to the 2:1 debt-to-equity thin capitalization limitation and must be charged at an arm's-length interest rate. The payer must withhold PRC corporate income tax at 10% on gross interest unless a lower treaty rate applies, in which case a valid Tax Residency Certificate and Form of treaty benefit application must be filed before payment.

field_by_field_filling_dissection.entry_description: Accounting profit from core dice manufacturing and trading after deducting cost of sales, operating expenses, selling expenses, administrative expenses, and financial expenses.
field_by_field_filling_dissection.non_resident_entry_guidance: Recompute operating profit after mandatory transfer pricing adjustments. Any unilateral price correction made by the WFOE through a compensating adjustment must be reported on the related-party transaction schedules and cannot alter the statutory tax computation absent approval of the tax authority.

field_by_field_filling_dissection.entry_description: Gains from disposal of non-current assets, government subsidies, insurance indemnities, inventory overage, and unreturned deposits belonging to third parties.
field_by_field_filling_dissection.non_resident_entry_guidance: Government subsidies received in connection with asset acquisition may be spread over the asset's depreciable life; subsidies compensating operating expenses are taxable in the year received. Cross-border shareholders' capital contributions are not non-operating income.

field_by_field_filling_dissection.entry_description: Asset write-downs, donations, fines other than penal tax surcharges, disaster losses, and inventory spoilage.
field_by_field_filling_dissection.non_resident_entry_guidance: Administrative penalties, tax penalties, and criminal fines are nondeductible. Public welfare donations are deductible only up to 12% of annual accounting profit and only if made through approved Chinese charitable institutions; direct donations to offshore charities are not deductible.

field_by_field_filling_dissection.line_or_box_code: Box 10 (Line 10: Total Accounting Profit/Loss Offset by Loss Carryforward)
field_by_field_filling_dissection.entry_description: Aggregate accounting profit or loss after non-operating items and before statutory tax adjustments, reduced by allowable qualified tax losses brought forward from prior years.
field_by_field_filling_dissection.non_resident_entry_guidance: Tax losses may be carried forward for 5 years, or 10 years for qualifying High and New Technology Enterprises or scientifically-oriented SMEs. Losses of a Chinese WFOE cannot be surrendered to a foreign parent and cannot be used by a non-resident shareholder to shelter China-source income.

field_by_field_filling_dissection.entry_description: Taxable income after adding non-deductible expenses, transfer pricing add-backs, thin capitalization disallowances, and other statutory adjustments, and after deducting tax holidays and preferential deductions.
field_by_field_filling_dissection.non_resident_entry_guidance: The WFOE must complete Schedule A105000 reconciling accounting profit to taxable income, including full disclosure of all related-party transactions. A failure to disclose cross-border transactions with the foreign parent will be treated as a serious reporting omission and trigger the initiation of a special tax investigation.

field_by_field_filling_dissection.line_or_box_code: Box 12 (Line 12: Tax Payable at Statutory or Preferential Rate)
field_by_field_filling_dissection.entry_description: Computed corporate income tax by applying 25% statutory rate, or 15% HNTE rate, or the 20% small low-profit enterprise rate to taxable income after applying the applicable preferential inclusion.
field_by_field_filling_dissection.non_resident_entry_guidance: A WFOE cannot flow through profits to foreign shareholders for individual rate purposes; the entity is taxed at the entity level. If the enterprise has foreign tax credits from Chinese-source income taxed abroad, attach the required credit certificates in the annual settlement before final payment is made.

field_by_field_filling_dissection.line_or_box_code: Box 13 (Line 13: Foreign Tax Credit and Other Credits)
field_by_field_filling_dissection.entry_description: Creditable foreign income taxes paid on foreign-source income received by the WFOE, including withholding taxes paid to jurisdictions where the WFOE carries on a trade.
field_by_field_filling_dissection.non_resident_entry_guidance: A foreign tax credit is allowed only to the extent of the PRC CIT payable on that foreign-source income and only when official proof of payment is provided. The WFOE must not claim foreign tax credits on dividend income that is exempt in China from a Chinese subsidiary.

field_by_field_filling_dissection.line_or_box_code: Box 14 (Withholding and Reporting of Non-Resident Payments)
field_by_field_filling_dissection.entry_description: Declaration of dividends, interest, royalties, rental fees, and service fees paid or credited to a non-resident company or individual, for which the WFOE acts as withholding agent.
field_by_field_filling_dissection.non_resident_entry_guidance: When distributing profits to a foreign corporate shareholder, the WFOE must withhold 10% on the gross dividend before remittance. To claim a lower treaty rate, the WFOE must obtain the beneficial owner certification, the Tax Residency Certificate, and file the application for treaty benefits with the State Administration of Taxation before the withholding tax return is filed.

tax_return_filing_anatomy.failure_penalties: Late filing of the quarterly or annual return attracts a penalty of RMB 2,000 per case, increased to RMB 10,000 for aggravated non-compliance. Late payment of tax creates a daily surcharge of 0.05% on the overdue amount. Underpayment resulting from inaccurate or fraudulent reporting is punishable by a fine of 50% to 500% of the tax evaded. Where the amount of tax evaded exceeds RMB 100,000 and exceeds 10% of the tax payable, the legal representative and directly responsible directors may face criminal prosecution under PRC Criminal Law Article 201, with imprisonment of up to 7 years for amounts that are especially huge.

profit_repatriation_and_withholding_tax.statutory_dividend_wht_rate: 10% withholding on outbound dividends paid by a PRC resident enterprise to a non-resident corporate shareholder, applied at the statutory 20% reduced income tax rate on dividends through the withholding mechanism under PRC Enterprise Income Tax Law Article 37 and implementing regulations.
profit_repatriation_and_withholding_tax.treaty_relief_application_protocol: To claim double tax treaty relief on dividends, the WFOE must submit a non-resident treaty benefit application to the competent PRC tax authorities before remittance, accompanied by: (1) a valid Tax Residency Certificate (TRC) issued by the tax authority of the shareholder's residence country for the calendar year in which the dividend is paid; (2) documentary proof that the shareholder is the beneficial owner of the dividend and not a conduit or agent; (3) evidence of direct shareholding satisfying the relevant DTA minimum participation threshold (for example, 25% direct capital for the Hong Kong-China arrangement); and (4) a declaration of absence of abuse of law or artificial arrangements. The tax bureau will issue a certificate of withholding reduction or exemption; remitting the dividend before approval risks full 10% withholding without later recovery.
profit_repatriation_and_withholding_tax.cross_border_royalty_and_interest_wht: Statutory PRC withholding tax on non-resident interest and royalties derived from sources within China is 10% for both categories. Under applicable bilateral double taxation treaties, interest may be reduced to between 5% and 7% and royalties to between 5% and 7%, subject to the non-resident being the beneficial owner and holding valid TRC documentation. Royalty payments for trademarks, patents, or know-how used in the dice-casting process, including licensing of moulds and resin formulas, must satisfy the arm's-length royalty rate and require contemporaneous intangible transfer pricing documentation.

transfer_pricing_and_economic_substance.tp_documentation_threshold_local_currenc: Mandatory Local File contemporaneous documentation is required when related-party tangible asset transfers exceed RMB 200 million in a single tax year, or when related-party transactions involving financial assets or intangible property exceed RMB 100 million in a single tax year. A Master File is required where the ultimate parent of the multinational group has annual consolidated revenue exceeding RMB 3 billion and the WFOE is participating in cross-border related-party transactions, as stipulated by SAT Announcement No. 42 of 2016.
transfer_pricing_and_economic_substance.economic_substance_doctrine: China does not apply a named Economic Substance Regulation in the style of offshore financial centres, but the PRC corporate income tax system mandates economic substance under Enterprise Income Tax Law Articles 41, 45, and 47. A WFOE manufacturing polyhedral dice must show genuine factory premises, production equipment, operational staff, managerial decision-making, and core income-generating activities in China. If the WFOE is a mere letterbox entity invoicing through the group, the general anti-avoidance rule allows the tax authority to recharacterize transactions, reallocate profit to the Chinese manufacturing site, impute a dividend to the foreign shareholder, and impose withholding taxes plus penalties.

fatal_compliance_red_flags_and_liabiliti.triggering_act: The WFOE repeatedly sold polyhedral dice to an affiliated Hong Kong distributor at a price below manufacturing cost or at a 25% discount from the price charged to independent third-party customers, thereby shifting pre-tax profit into a low-tax jurisdiction.
fatal_compliance_red_flags_and_liabiliti.statutory_sanction: PRC Enterprise Income Tax Law Article 41 (transfer pricing adjustment), Article 44 (presumptive assessment), and Tax Collection Administration Law Article 63: the tax authority may recharacterize the transaction, impose additional corporate income tax at 25%, charge a daily late-payment surcharge of 0.05%, and impose a penalty of 50% to 500% of the underpaid tax. Where the evasion is intentional and exceeds the criminal threshold, PRC Criminal Law Article 201 imposes criminal liability for fraudulent tax reporting.
fatal_compliance_red_flags_and_liabiliti.personal_liability_of_directors: If the director or legal representative instructed the underpricing to a related foreign entity, the corporate veil may be pierced under PRC Company Law Article 20 (successor Article 23 of the 2023 Company Law), making the director personally liable for the unpaid corporate tax and civil restitution. The director may be placed on the State Administration of Taxation blacklist, banned from leaving China, prohibited from high-consumption travel, and, upon criminal conviction, sentenced to up to 3 years imprisonment for ordinary tax evasion or 3 to 7 years where the amount of tax evaded is especially enormous.

fatal_compliance_red_flags_and_liabiliti.infraction_category: Withholding Tax Evasion / Disguised Profit Distribution
fatal_compliance_red_flags_and_liabiliti.triggering_act: The WFOE executed a fabricated trademark license and technical consulting agreement with its offshore parent, paying inflated royalties for a resin formula and trademark never used in the actual dice-casting operation, thereby disguising a dividend and avoiding the 10% statutory withholding tax on outbound dividends.
fatal_compliance_red_flags_and_liabiliti.statutory_sanction: PRC Enterprise Income Tax Law Articles 3, 37, 41, and 47; Tax Collection Administration Law Article 69: a withholding agent that fails to withhold is subject to a penalty equal to 50% to 300% of the tax not withheld. The payments will be recharacterized as dividends sourced in China and taxed at 10% gross, in addition to the penalty.
fatal_compliance_red_flags_and_liabiliti.personal_liability_of_directors: Directors who signed the fictitious licensing documents face personal civil liability for the withheld tax, interest, and penalties. Where the tribunal finds intentional evasion of withholding, the director may be subject to criminal prosecution under PRC Criminal Law Article 201, asset freezing, exit bans, and disqualification from acting as a company director for a specified period.

fatal_compliance_red_flags_and_liabiliti.infraction_category: Shell Company / GAAR and Falsified Export Mechanics
fatal_compliance_red_flags_and_liabiliti.triggering_act: The WFOE was registered at a post-office address with no factory floor, no production personnel, and no physical raw materials, yet issued commercial invoices for manufactured dice, claimed preferential small-low-profit CIT treatment, filed for VAT export refunds, and asserted treaty benefits on remitted profits, without any actual manufacturing activity or movement of the goods.
fatal_compliance_red_flags_and_liabiliti.statutory_sanction: PRC Enterprise Income Tax Law Article 47 (GAAR), Article 44 (deemed assessment), Tax Collection Administration Law Articles 34, 63, and 66, and PRC Criminal Law Articles 204 and 205: false export refunds and fictitious VAT invoices are punishable by severe financial penalties, confiscation of illegal gains, forced refund, interest, and fines up to 5 times the tax involved; the criminal maximum for particularly large fraudulent VAT or export rebate cases may be life imprisonment.
fatal_compliance_red_flags_and_liabiliti.personal_liability_of_directors: The court may disregard the corporate limited liability and pierce the veil under PRC Company Law Article 20/23 where the corporation is used as a vehicle for fraud. Directors are personally liable for the restitution of all refunded taxes and public funds; the Public Security Bureau may impose travel bans and blacklist the legal representative; the person may also be barred from leaving China under the exit-restriction notice system and may face criminal detention or imprisonment, in serious cases exceeding 10 years or life imprisonment, with personal assets subject to confiscation.
